study_identification_part.si_4_title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to model the development of absolute and relative tissue volumes in the control sample from 32 to 46 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) at scan. GPR modeling was implemented using GPy in Python. GPR is a Bayesian non-parametric regression method that provides a point estimate of the average volume and measures of predictive confidence for every observation, while accounting for modeled covariates.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to model the development of absolute and relative tissue volumes in the control sample from 32 to 46 weeks PMA at scan. GPR modeling was implemented using GPy in Python (https://sheffieldml.github.io/GPy/; accessed 2021 November 15) as per (Bonthrone et al. 2021; Dimitrova et al. 2021). GPR is a Bayesian non-parametric regression method that provides a point estimate of the average volume and measures of predictive confidence for every observation, whereas accounting for modeled covariates.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: FukamiGartner2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling using Gaussian process regression

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional brain tissue volumes were modeled, including: intracranial volume (ICV), total brain volume (TBV), total tissue volume (TTV), total cortical gray matter (GM), total white matter (WM), deep GM (caudate nucleus, lentiform nucleus, thalamus), cerebellum, brainstem, lateral ventricles, extra-cerebral CSF (eCSF), hippocampus, amygdala, and lobar volumes (frontal, temporal, parietal, occipital, insula, cingulate - each for GM and WM separately). Both absolute volumes (in cm3) and relative volumes (proportional to whole brain measures) were extracted.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: T2-weighted images were segmented into seven main tissue classes: extra-cerebral cerebrospinal fluid (eCSF), lateral ventricles, cortical GM, WM, deep GM, cerebellum, and brainstem (hereafter referred to as 'main tissue classes'). [...] Cortical GM, deep GM, and WM were further automatically segmented into the specific tissue segments listed in Table 1. [...] Tissue segments were used to extract absolute (in cm3) and relative (i.e. proportional) volumes.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: FukamiGartner2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / MR image segmentation; Table 1

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Three covariates were used in the GPR normative model: (1) Sex - male or female; (2) PMA at scan (postmenstrual age at scan in weeks) - ranging from 32 to 46 weeks; (3) Age from birth (in weeks) - the time elapsed from birth to the scan. These variables were used to account for developmental variation when extracting individualized z-scores for the Down syndrome sample.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Subsequently, the GPR model was used to extract individualized absolute and relative volume z-scores (by segment, as listed in Table 1) for an independent sample of 25 neonates with DS, accounting for sex, PMA at scan (in weeks), and age from birth (in weeks) variables.
